name: Dai Yem Waterfall
kicker: Two limestone drops you hear before you see
summary: Go for the two limestone drops at Ban Vat, the fall you hear before you see it. Vietnam Tourism puts the drop over 100 m. The heritage monograph puts the first fall at about 70 m. The two figures do not match. Check the gate. Skip it when the tea rows are the only morning you wanted.
getThere: From the farm town on National Highway 43. The two route descriptions disagree.
heroCaption: The wide falls, the limestone, and the pool under the lower water

notice.title: The published heights do not agree
notice.body: Vietnam Tourism says the drop is over 100 m. The 2011 monograph says the first fall drops about 70 m, in three tiers. Do not treat those as one number. The fee is check on arrival.

body: Walk down to the limestone falls at Ban Vat. The water comes in two parts, with a pool under the lower drop. Vietnam Tourism says you hear it before you see it. A red Love Glass Bridge crosses above the falls on that page. The 2011 monograph describes stair paths and does not mention the bridge. The bridge is the later feature.

Do not leave with one height. Vietnam Tourism says the drop is over 100 m. The monograph says the first fall drops about 70 m and is in three tiers, with a first tier about 40 m deep, about 70 m wide, and about 50 m high, and puts the two falls about 200 m apart. The national page puts the two falls 150 m apart and describes a sheet about 70 m wide when the water is full.

The national page calls the water fullest from April to September. The monograph says May to September for the first fall’s lip and April to September for the second. An 18 Jan 2022 decision recognizes the site as a provincial eco site and prints no tariff. The fee, the hours, and how long you stay are check on arrival.

figures.caption: The lip and the sheet, from under the fall
figures.alt: White water leaving a dark rock lip at Dai Yem, with forest on both sides

gettingThere: The falls are at Bản Vặt, xã Mường Sang, on National Highway 43. A 2022 provincial row still uses that address. Ward names after 2025 are check on arrival.

The monograph gives two drives. Toward Son La, about 3 km on National Highway 6 to the Long Sap junction, then left about 5 km on National Highway 43. Toward Hanoi, about 1 km to that junction, then right about 5 km. The national page says 3 km from the farm town, and also about 4 km from the Pa Hang junction. The two descriptions do not match. Minutes are check on arrival.
